cards.text: Once again the Philistines go to war against Israel, and David and his servants go down and fight them. And then the king gets EXHAUSTED. Friend, I get winded pressing one tray of dough, so I am not judging anybody.
Then here comes Ishbi-benob, a descendant of Rapha, with a bronze spear that weighs three hundred shekels and a brand NEW sword. And the king is already out of breath. Oh, this is TERRIBLE timing.

cards.question: With David worn out, what is Ishbi-benob set on doing?
David is exhausted, and Ishbi-benob is coming for him. Who comes to David's aid?

cards.text: Abishai son of Zeruiah, one of David's fighting men, strikes the Philistine and kills him. Then David's men gather around their king with something serious to say.

cards.question: After that close call, what do David's men swear to him?

answers.text: He must never go to battle with them again
They will always fight right beside him
He must lead them from the very front

cards.text: Their reason: "so that the lamp of Israel may not be extinguished." Friend, that is the most beautiful way anybody has ever said "Sir, please SIT DOWN."
Some time later, there's another battle with the Philistines, this time at Gob. Sibbecai the Hushathite kills a man named Saph.

cards.question: Like Ishbi-benob, Saph is a descendant of Rapha.

cards.text: Then there's ANOTHER battle at Gob, because apparently Gob is where everybody meets up now. Elhanan son of Jair the Bethlehemite kills the brother of a famous Philistine, and this verse has a spear in it with a shaft like a weaver's beam.

cards.question: At Gob, Elhanan son of Jair kills the brother of which famous Philistine?

cards.text: Next comes a battle at Gath, with a man of great stature. And this man has something unusual going on with his hands and feet.

cards.question: What stands out about the hands and feet of the man of great stature at Gath?

answers.text: He has six fingers and six toes on each
He wears bronze armor on each of them
He carries a sword in each of his hands

cards.text: Six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot, twenty-four in all, and here I am with a MUSTACHE for hands, feeling some kind of way. He too is descended from Rapha.

cards.question: The man of great stature at Gath ___ Israel.
When the man at Gath taunts Israel, who kills him?

answers.text: Jonathan son of David's brother Shimei
Amasa son of David's sister Abigail
Absalom son of David's wife Maacah

cards.question: Counting every battle in this passage, how many descendants of Rapha fall?

cards.text: So these four descendants of Rapha in Gath fall at the hands of David and his servants. My backup in the junk drawer was a couple of dead batteries swearing they still had a little charge left, so friend, I am JEALOUS of David's team.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: Ishbi-benob arriving with his spear and sword, the king being out of breath, and the 'TERRIBLE timing' line. Only the opening card can run to 3 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Card 12 says the man has something unusual going on with his hands and feet. The wrong answer 'He carries a sword in each of his hands' covers only the hands, so a baker can rule it out from the setup. A wrong answer about both hands and feet would not have this problem.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The right answer 'He has six fingers and six toes on each' can be read as six fingers and six toes on each hand and foot. The text says six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot (2 Samuel 21:20).

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The joke is built on the man's physical trait (six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot), compared with Papa Dorin's mustache for hands. The humor is self-deprecating and doesn't mock the man, but its premise is a Bible person's body.
findings.question: Hard rules say 'Never puts down any person or group: no jokes about ... appearance.' Does that ban only jokes that put someone down, or any joke about a Bible person's physical appearance, even a self-deprecating comparison like this one?
